research_goal: mitigate losses and improve entry accuracy/continuation quality before optimizing profitability
scientific_caveat: May-Jul activity-anchor failure had already been examined during post-mortem before this exact owner was durably frozen. Model/rule selection used Jan-Mar discovery and April calibration only, but May-Jul should be treated as repeated forward diagnostic rather than pristine holdout. Do not assign R9B_Gamma_2 without a fresh certification gate.

diagnosis.primary_failure: winner compression / continuation failure, not a simple win-rate collapse or exploding average loss
interpretation: The 256-tick anchor became much slower in physical time during July, making the reference level older and first-break entries less continuation-capable.
Most entries still achieved the first +$0.10 activation, but far fewer extended to +$0.20/+0.30, so the system harvested many small winners while still carrying materially larger losers.
Quick sweep/reclaim events remained only ~17-18% of trades but generated roughly 39-42% of gross loss; this is a persistent structural loss population.
Simple higher-timeframe vote count did not solve July; regime ownership must be state-specific rather than another majority-vote filter.

deterministic_logic: if 1.426750 < displacement <= 2.502500 and signal_delay_s <= 1.663500, require range_atr <= 0.194659
interpretation: instantaneous strong/wide spike treated as possible exhaustion/sweep

threshold_plateau: Exact threshold stress at 0.51, 0.52 and 0.54 produced identical monthly results; 0.56 was nearly identical and slightly more selective. This is a discrete leaf plateau rather than a single numeric point.
